data.name: Sabrina
data.long_meaning:
In Hebrew, Sabrina means 'sorceress'. In Greek mythology, Sabrina is the Roman goddess of the Wetlands and the personification of the River Severn.
In Christian tradition, Sabrina can be associated with St. Sabina, an early Christian martyr whose relics were discovered in the catacombs of Rome. She is believed to have been a servant girl who was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian (284-305 AD).

in_hebrew.name: סברינה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: סברינה הוא שם שמקורו בנהר סברין, אחד הנהרות החשובים באנגליה. השם מתקשר ליופי, טוהר וקורנה. בקרב הנוצרים, השם מייצג את היופי והאור של אלוהים. השם סברינה משמש גם כזכר לנהר סברין, המסמל את החיים והזרימה הרוחנית.

in_greek.name: Σαβρίνη
in_greek.meaning: Από τον ποταμό Σαβρίνη, όμορφη και λαμπρή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Σαβρίνη είναι όνομα που συνδέεται με τον ποταμό Σαβρίνη, ένα από τους σημαντικότερους ποταμούς στην Αγγλία. Το όνομα σχετίζεται με την ομορφιά, την καθαρότητα και το φως. Ανάμεσα στους Χριστιανούς, το Σαβρίνη αντιπροσωπεύει την ομορφιά και το φως του Θεού. Το Σαβρίνη χρησιμεύει επίσης ως ανάμνηση του ποταμού Σαβρίνη, που συμβολίζει τη ζωή και τη ροή του πνεύματος.

seo.title: Sabrina: The Hebrew Sorceress and Christian Martyr
seo.meta_description: Discover the meaning and religious significance of the name Sabrina, derived from its Hebrew origins and Greek mythology. Also learn about its Christian association with St. Sabina, a revered martyr.
seo.description_paragraph:
Sabrina, a name of Hebrew origin, is a fascinating combination of mythology, history, and religious significance. In Hebrew, the name means 'sorceress', a nod to the mystical and magical powers often associated with the name. However, Sabrina's meaning extends beyond its Hebrew roots, as it is also associated with the Greek goddess Sabrina and the Christian martyr St. Sabina.
According to Greek mythology, Sabrina is the Roman goddess of the Wetlands and the personification of the River Severn. In this context, the name evokes images of water, renewal, and life. In Christian tradition, Sabrina takes on a different meaning as it is associated with St. Sabina, an early Christian martyr who was discovered in the catacombs of Rome.
Born as a servant girl, St. Sabina was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian (284-305 AD). Her bravery and unwavering faith in the face of adversity have made her a revered figure in the Christian faith. Sabrina, as a name, carries with it the legacy of this brave and inspiring woman, reminding us of the power of faith and perseverance.
